rows.source: HSE older-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Employers have the same health and safety responsibilities for older workers as for all other workers.

rows.source: HSE older-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: A separate risk assessment is not required solely because a worker reaches a particular age.

rows.source: HSE older-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Risk assessments should be reviewed when something significant changes and should consider the activities older workers perform.

rows.source: HSE older-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Employers should avoid assumptions and consult older workers when considering control measures.

rows.source: HSE older-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Older workers may benefit from more time to absorb health and safety information or from self-paced training.

rows.source: HSE older-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Employers can consider opportunities for older workers to choose other types of work where appropriate.

rows.source: HSE older-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Manual-handling tasks should be designed to eliminate or minimise risk rather than assuming older workers cannot perform demanding work.

rows.source: HSE older-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Technology can reduce physical strain and structured work with colleagues can capture older workers' knowledge and experience.

rows.source: HSE older-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Older-worker risk depends on individual capability and health, task design, physical demand, training method, working pattern, workplace change and available technology.

rows.source: HSE older-worker health and safety guidance
rows.verified: General age-neutral assessment, consultation, training, work design and use of experience guidance does not prove the current condition, exposure or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact event or illness probability.

rows.source: HSE disabled-worker and reasonable-adjustment guidance
rows.verified: Health and safety law should not be used as an excuse to discriminate against disabled workers or prevent them entering or remaining in work.

rows.source: HSE disabled-worker and reasonable-adjustment guidance
rows.verified: Employers are responsible for the health, safety and welfare of all employees whether or not they have a disability.

rows.source: HSE disabled-worker and reasonable-adjustment guidance
rows.verified: There is no general requirement for a separate disability-specific risk assessment, but the existing assessment should be reviewed when relevant disability needs become known.

rows.source: HSE disabled-worker and reasonable-adjustment guidance
rows.verified: Employers should avoid assumptions and blanket restrictions because disabilities affect people individually.

rows.source: HSE disabled-worker and reasonable-adjustment guidance
rows.verified: Employers have a duty to make reasonable adjustments so disabled workers have comparable access to obtaining and keeping work.

rows.source: HSE disabled-worker and reasonable-adjustment guidance
rows.verified: Adjustments can remove physical barriers, change layout, adapt equipment or provide additional support.

rows.source: HSE disabled-worker and reasonable-adjustment guidance
rows.verified: Risk can sometimes be managed by reallocating tasks, rescheduling duties or providing suitable alternative equipment.

rows.source: HSE disabled-worker and reasonable-adjustment guidance
rows.verified: Workers are not obliged to disclose disability details, and employers should involve them and obtain consent before seeking specialist information.

rows.source: HSE disabled-worker and reasonable-adjustment guidance
rows.verified: Disabled-worker risk and adjustment needs depend on the individual, impairment effects, task, environment, communication, equipment, barriers and agreed support.

rows.source: HSE disabled-worker and reasonable-adjustment guidance
rows.verified: General inclusive risk assessment, individual consultation, adjustments, specialist advice and disclosure guidance does not prove the current condition, exposure or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact event or illness probability.
